current_leader.name: Processor native-currency settlement optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: foreign-currency processor balance is created -> account lacks or underuses matching settlement currency -> processor converts to default currency or merchant later reconverts for same-currency obligations -> compare native-settlement payout fee, forced-conversion cost and forecast same-currency spend -> recommend native settlement only where deterministic fee delta is positive -> avoid unnecessary FX conversions
current_leader.why_survived: Stripe documents that payout in a currency with a matching bank account causes no conversion, while balances without a matching settlement account are converted to the default currency. Current pricing explicitly attaches percentage fees to multi-currency settlement and currency conversion, making the decision measurable. A tiny read-only layer can compare processor balances and fee tables with same-currency upcoming obligations and recommend native settlement only where it wins. Broad treasury/FX platforms are adjacent, but no exact lightweight merchant-side product was found that continuously performs this PSP-specific native-vs-convert decision without executing trades or owning the rail.
current_leader.closest_threat: Kantox, Pleo and LimFi already optimize FX, multi-currency balances and netting, while Stripe itself exposes native-currency settlement. The wedge only survives if the recurring PSP-specific decision adds material value beyond a one-time multi-currency account setup.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read-only v1: ingest PSP balances by currency, configured settlement accounts, PSP conversion/payout fee tables, and authorized upcoming AP/card obligations by currency; output which currencies should settle natively versus convert, with deterministic expected savings. Do not initiate payouts, conversions or hold funds.
current_leader.monetization: Small per-currency optimization fee, monthly fee, or capped share of verified processor FX fees avoided, benchmarked against competent static configuration and inexpensive treasury tools.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The best configuration may be stable and obvious after a one-time setup. If two or three matching currency accounts capture most of the savings permanently, recurring monetization fails despite real leakage.
current_leader.next_research_test: Attack recurrence and exact competition. Quantify merchant PSP FX leakage after competent static multi-currency setup; determine whether changing currency mix and same-currency obligations frequently alter the optimal configuration; search exact products combining PSP balances, fee schedules and external obligations to recommend native-vs-convert per currency. Kill if one-time configuration captures most value or a sufficiently close incumbent exists.

recent_cross_family_findings: Processor-native currency settlement creates a machine-readable convert-vs-native fee decision: matching settlement accounts can avoid processor conversion, but native settlement itself may carry a payout fee.
The true recurring value must be measured after competent static multi-currency setup; one-time configuration savings do not justify a recurring optimizer.
Kantox, Pleo and LimFi materially increase Gate-8 risk because they already automate broader FX exposure, multi-currency balances and netting.
App-store subscription price-consent optimization is demoted because revenue delta depends on churn counterfactuals and current pricing tools already flag consent-risk thresholds.
Warranty parts returns, telecom pooled-plan right-sizing and healthcare timely-filing prioritization are occupied by dedicated software and should not be revived without materially new evidence.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
